newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan law to target smugglers of illegal workers.
newsitem.headline: Japan law to target smugglers of illegal workers.

text.p: The Japanese government submitted to parliament on Friday legislation to boost the maximum jail term to 10 years from 18 months for those trying to smuggle workers into the country.

In a further crackdown on syndicates involved in human smuggling, the fines for such offences will rise to a maximum of 10 million yen ($81,300) from 150,000 yen ($1,220), the government said in a statement.
The proposed revisions to the Immigration Control Law were approved at a cabinet meeting on Friday and sent to parliament.
No parties were opposed to the move and it was expected to be passed by parliament later this month.
Under current law, organisers of the smuggling rings face lighter punishment than the illegal entrants themselves.
"We hope these stiff penalties will be a deterrent against the current rush of illegal immigrants," a Justice Ministry spokesman said.
In the first two months of this year a record 581 illegal Chinese immigrants were arrested by Japanese authorities, already exceeding last year's total of 545 people.
The brokers are known as "Snakeheads" for their reputed viciousness and the problems faced in countering them.
Many illegal immigrants have tried to enter Japan in boats from Fujian and other densely populated coastal areas of China, lured by the prospect of high wages in Japan.
In the first crackdown this year on groups suspected of organising the boat trips, Japanese police in February arrested seven suspected members of a Japan-based gang of Chinese smugglers.
